text:
marta: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a 'compat backstop' for major API migrations. Lightweight shim that accepts old vX shapes and translates to vY, emits deprecation telemetry and a migration hint header. Goal: avoid customer breakage during cutover windows. Thoughts?
ryan: sounds useful. main question: latency overhead and where it lives (edge vs runtime)?
samir: can we make it opt-in by tenant? don't want everyone paying the cost.
eva: also need emergency kill switch if shim misbehaves during peak.
marta: proposed rollout waves: 1) opt-in sidecar for early adopters, 2) global opt-in feature-flag (rate-limited) for migration ramp, 3) sunsetting clients. Each wave 6 weeks with canaries + metrics.
ryan: can you sketch the translation contract? how do we handle extra fields or removed semantics?
marta: translator rules are simple: map request envelope, normalize renamed fields, reject incompatible combos with clear error + migration hint. We'll preserve request-id and auth.
samir: telemetry we should emit: compat.shim.hit, compat.shim.latency_ms, compat.shim.translate_errors. Also record tenant.optin boolean.
eva: streaming is hairy — framing and chunk semantics differ. Are we supporting streaming in wave 1?
marta: initial shim will support unary endpoints and a minimal streaming wrapper that envelopes legacy frames to our new frame type. Not full parity initially, documented as "best-effort".
ryan: need to be explicit about billing: shim must not double-count tokens or change billing metrics.
samir: agree — translation should be zero-cost in billing pipeline: pass-through token counts to billing service.
marta: ownership: infra/eng-runtime implement shim runtime; product + eng-platform own the rollout policy and migration UX (headers, client hints).
eva: add runbook items: SLO delta threshold to trigger rollback, error budget alarms, and a smoke test that validates parity on a small prompt set.
marta: migration hint header idea: X-Redwood-Migrate-To: vY; also X-Redwood-Compat-Mode: translate/strict. Clients can detect and auto-upgrade.
ryan: can we provide client-side opt-in helpers in SDKs? small function to detect header and auto-switch.
marta: yes — shipping SDK helpers is part of the plan.
samir: implementation detail: where to place the shim? options: edge lambda (low-latency), sidecar next to runtime (higher throughput), or central translation service (simpler). My preference: sidecar per-runtime pool for stateful adjustments and caching.
eva: sidecar seems safer for streaming, but edges are better for low-latency for small requests. Maybe hybrid: edge for unary, sidecar for streaming heavy paths.
ryan: agree hybrid, but adds complexity in routing. Need routing policy in smart-router to prefer edge when available.
marta: canary checklist: 1) deploy shim to 3 tenants, 2) enable opt-in via header, 3) compare outputs vs native vY for parity metrics, 4) monitor latency, token counts, error rates.
samir: rollout toggles: per-tenant opt-in flag in feature-flags service; global override for incidents. I'll wire flags and telemetry tags.
eva: add a migration TTL for cached entries and KV-caching implications. Also ensure KV cache keys are normalized so translated requests hit the same cache when appropriate.
marta: good point — add cache-normalization rules to RFC addendum.
ryan: test matrix to include streaming chunk order, EOF handling, and tool-calling frames.
marta: will draft RFC addendum with these details and a small POC. Target: canary in ~2 weeks.
samir: I'll queue a spike for sidecar perf numbers this sprint.
eva: I'll draft the runbook and rollback triggers.
marta: quick example request to opt-in:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "X-Compat-Optin: true" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Compat-Mode: translate" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/legacy -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
samir: also accept query param ?compat=1 for clients that can't set headers.
ryan: let's make sure SDKs set a grace period where they warn on console when receiving X-Redwood-Migrate-To. Good UX.
marta: agreed. I'll include SDK upgrade helpers in the RFC.
eva: one last thing — add synthetic regression checks that run on every deploy and compare shim vs native outputs for a small seed corpus.
marta: will add that too. Thanks everyone, I'll post the RFC addendum tomorrow for review. :thumbsup:
